_what: Rail routes as the Board of Supervisors described them: a sequence of STREET NAMES, a date, and the words it was written in.
_how: Each route is a list of streets, copied from the ordinance, claim or contract
quoted beside it. build_rail_history.py resolves each name against DataSF's
street centrelines and stitches the geometry. Nothing here is drawn or traced;
the only thing being asserted is WHICH STREETS a line ran on and WHEN.
`streets` is the ordered list the record gives. `quote` is verbatim OCR from the
volume named in `source`, lightly de-hyphenated where the scan broke a word.
A route whose street cannot be resolved is REPORTED, never silently shortened --
a renamed or vanished street is a real gap and hiding it would make the map lie
_status: first pass: the municipally built lines, whose construction the Board paid for and therefore described. The private companies -- United Railroads and the Market Street Railway, most of the mileage -- are in FRANCHISE ordinances and are not here yet.

routes.name: Church street line (J)
routes.quote: For construction of Church street line, from Market street and Van Ness avenue to Sixteenth and Church streets, Section "A", Contract No. 23

routes.name: Twin Peaks tunnel line, Taraval extension (L)
routes.quote: Ordinance No. 4527 (New Series), approved by the Mayor September 25, 1917, providing for the construction of a line from the southwesterly portal of the Twin Peaks tunnel over Ulloa street, Fifteenth avenue and Taraval street to Twentieth avenue
routes.from_note: the ordinance's terminus is 'the southwesterly portal of the Twin Peaks tunnel', which is a place and not a street. West Portal Avenue is the street at that portal and is named for it. This is the one INTERPRETATION in the file and it is marked: without it the run along Ulloa has no start and falls back to an arbitrary length.

routes.name: Geary Street Municipal Railway, Richmond extension
routes.quote: J. R. No. 307. Resolved, That the Board of Public Works, be and it is hereby authorized and directed to advertise for bids for track construction for the Geary Street Municipal Railway from Geary street along Thirty-third avenue, Balboa street, Forty-fifth avenue and Cabrillo street to the Great Highway, and when bids shall have been received the Finance Committee will recommend the necessary appropriation.
routes.note: Muni's OWN FIRST LINE and a vanished one: Geary carries no rail today, so this route exists on the map only because the Board wrote it down. It should score LOW against the surviving network, and that is the point of it.
routes.ended_searched: No abandonment for the Geary line is in this corpus. Searched: the 1955 and 1956 volumes for abandon/discontinue/remove-tracks/motor-coach near 'Geary' (nothing), and 1953/1954 for conversion language. 1953 carries only a BOND PROPOSAL -- 'Extension of No. 8 Trolley Coach Line and Conversion of B and J Lines to Trolley Coach Operation' -- and a proposal is not a conversion. The same sentence names the J, which was never converted and runs as rail today, so the proposal cannot be read as a record of what happened. The line is gone (0.0 % against today's network) and this record does not say when, so it carries no `ended`.

_dropped: Ocean View line (M): its quote is a CONSTRUCTION PAYMENT and carries no street sequence. The streets first listed here were recalled rather than read, which is the exact failure this file exists to prevent, so the route is out until an ordinance describing it is found.
_ended: A route may carry `ended`: the year the Board authorised the tracks to be
TAKEN UP. Until now every layer on this map only ever grew, because today's
registers describe what survived. An abandonment ordinance is the other half
and it is in the same record.
`year` 0 on an abandoned route means the Journal proves the track EXISTED by
the year it was removed and does not say when it was laid -- so it is drawn
from the first frame, `streets.ts`'s own convention for a silent record.
That is a floor, not a claim about the year it was built.
_corpus_exhausted: The Board's Journal stops being useful for rail routes after 1951. The 1953, 1954, 1957 and 1958 volumes contain NO 'street railway track' or 'removal of track' phrasing at all -- by then the conversions were Public Utilities Commission decisions and the Board's record carries bond issues and debate rather than route descriptions. Harvested and empty, so nobody searches them twice: 1913, 1914, 1920, 1926(v21), 1948(v43), 1949(v44), 1953(v48), 1954(v49), 1957(v52), 1958(v53).
